findings.title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Each entry is `import("./x")`, a promise created as soon as the module is evaluated. All ~29 app packages are therefore loaded at once whenever `@calcom/app-store` is imported. That defeats the purpose of an async/lazy import. It also means a failure in any single app's module (for example a missing env var at import time) produces a rejected promise at startup. That rejection is unhandled until something awaits it. Entries should be thunks such as `() => import(...)`, called only for the app that is needed.

findings.title: getCalendar promise stored without handling, can reject unobserved
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still synchronous and now stores the unawaited promise from `getCalendar` as `calendar`. Any consumer that does not await it, or that filters out entries, leaves a rejected promise unobserved. Other callers using `calendar` from this result, outside `getConnectedCalendars`, will also receive a Promise instead of a Calendar, and TypeScript may not flag every use.

findings.title: async forEach callback is not awaited; errors escape try/catch
findings.body: The `forEach(async ...)` callback returns promises that nothing awaits, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures. A rejection from `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The function also proceeds to send emails and return before the calendar and video deletions finish. In serverless environments the work may be cut off. The same pattern is in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and trpc bookings.tsx. Use `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))`.

findings.title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch, `forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` before pushing into `apiDeletes`. The `apiDeletes` array is passed to `Promise.all` immediately afterwards, so these deletions are pushed too late and are never awaited. Recurring calendar events may not be deleted before the handler returns, and errors become unhandled rejections. Before this change the callback ran synchronously up to the first await. Use a `for...of` loop with `await`, as was done in the else branch.
